theme: FCI-JCI against pcalg 2.7-12's fci with jci, the implementation by the method's authors; BOSS-FCI and GRaSP-FCI against tetrad-lib 7.6.10's BossFci and GraspFci, the implementation by the methods' authors, with causal-cmd 1.12.0 (tetrad-lib 7.6.3) as context, and Andrey with edge_removal="triangles" against causal-cmd 1.12.0, which runs that rule; J-PCMCI+ against tigramite 5.2.10.1's JPCMCIplus, the implementation in the package of the method's authors
build: FCI-JCI: Andrey pre-release build of 6 November 2026 (version string 0.14.0); refitted on the 0.15.0 release branch of the same day, Andrey's two gated arms returned the same PAG on all 720 fits | BOSS-FCI/GRaSP-FCI: Andrey pre-release build of 7 November 2026 (version string 0.14.0), the 0.15.0 release branch, where BOSS-FCI and GRaSP-FCI follow the BOSS-FCI paper's Algorithm 5 by default; the option entries ran on the same branch with edge_removal="triangles" | J-PCMCI+: Andrey pre-release build of 8 November 2026 (version string 0.15.0); refitted on the 0.15.0 release branch, Andrey's arm returned the same graph on all 1,760 fits of the linear cells
verdict_rule: FCI-JCI: per cell, assumption set (jci = "1" with confounded_index=True, jci = "123" with confounded_index=False), and level: D = SHD(Andrey) - SHD(pcalg) per dataset, on the datasets both finished; worse when the 95% percentile-bootstrap interval of mean D lies entirely above 0, better when entirely below, a tie otherwise; a row with fewer than 10 paired datasets is reported, not judged; better or worse counts only if a rerun on seeds 100-119 agrees. 10,000 resamples of the datasets, default_rng(0). An in-claim row also fails when Andrey timed out on a dataset pcalg finished. Floor, in every row that records one (floor): andrey_minus_empty is the 95% interval of the mean of Andrey's error minus the empty estimate's (the empty graph, or for a target error the given targets alone, or no targets), and reference_minus_empty the same for the reference; the floor applies only where the reference's interval lies wholly below 0, where the reference itself beats the empty estimate, and there Andrey's interval must lie wholly below 0 too; elsewhere it is reported as not applied (applies false), with its numbers. The floor is judged on the first seeds; a replication's floor (the rerun on fresh seeds) only confirms a failure there | BOSS-FCI/GRaSP-FCI: per cell, method, and setting: D = SHD(Andrey) - SHD(reference) per dataset, the reference's SHD the mean over its runs on that dataset, on the datasets both finished; worse when the 95% percentile-bootstrap interval of mean D lies entirely above 0, better when entirely below, a tie otherwise; a row with fewer than 10 paired datasets is reported, not judged; better or worse counts only if a rerun on seeds 100-119 agrees. 10,000 resamples of the datasets, default_rng(0). tetrad-lib 7.6.10's BossFci and GraspFci are the gated reference; causal-cmd 1.12.0's bfci and grasp-fci (tetrad-lib 7.6.3) are context (role), reported and never judged; Andrey's boss_fci and grasp_fci with edge_removal="triangles", the rule of Ogarrio, Spirtes, and Ramsey (2016, Sec. 5) that causal-cmd 1.12.0 (tetrad-lib 7.6.3) runs, are judged against causal-cmd's bfci and grasp-fci by the same rule (the entries whose comparator is Tetrad 7.6.3; role option in the lane file), on the in-claim cells; the default rows stay against tetrad-lib 7.6.10. Floor, in every row that records one (floor): andrey_minus_empty is the 95% interval of the mean of Andrey's error minus the empty estimate's (the empty graph, or for a target error the given targets alone, or no targets), and reference_minus_empty the same for the reference; the floor applies only where the reference's interval lies wholly below 0, where the reference itself beats the empty estimate, and there Andrey's interval must lie wholly below 0 too; elsewhere it is reported as not applied (applies false), with its numbers. The floor is judged on the first seeds; a replication's floor (the rerun on fresh seeds) only confirms a failure there | J-PCMCI+: per cell, level, and error: D = error(Andrey) - error(tigramite) per draw (one seed's datasets), on the draws both finished; worse when the 95% percentile-bootstrap interval of mean D lies entirely above 0, better when entirely below, a tie otherwise; a row with fewer than 10 paired datasets is reported, not judged. 10,000 resamples of the draws, default_rng(0). The claim is judged at alpha 0.05, the paper's level, on the system SHD of every claimed cell and the context error where every context is observed; in a cell with a hidden context, the draws where a hidden context confounds an observed context and a system variable (Assumption 3 broken) form a row of their own, reported, not judged. Better or worse counts only if a rerun on fresh seeds agrees. An in-claim row also fails when an Andrey fit did not finish where tigramite's did. Floor, in every row that records one (floor): andrey_minus_empty is the 95% interval of the mean of Andrey's error minus the empty estimate's (the empty graph, or for a target error the given targets alone, or no targets), and reference_minus_empty the same for the reference; the floor applies only where the reference's interval lies wholly below 0, where the reference itself beats the empty estimate, and there Andrey's interval must lie wholly below 0 too; elsewhere it is reported as not applied (applies false), with its numbers. The floor is judged on the first seeds; a replication's floor (the rerun on fresh seeds) only confirms a failure there
card_verdict_rule: card_verdict, on every row: the release card's verdict on the row's comparison, 'better', 'tie', or 'worse', and null where the card judges none (rows out of claim, and rows with fewer than 10 paired datasets). Better or worse counts only where a rerun on fresh seeds agreed; one on the first seeds alone is a tie
fit_protocol: FCI-JCI: each fit in a fresh interpreter on one core with one BLAS thread, after one untimed warm-up fit (pcalg's warm-up only at 4 and 10 variables, where it cannot double a fit that may reach the cap); a cap of 1,800 s per fit with imports and warm-up, past which a fit is a timeout, never an empty graph; Andrey's time runs from the array in memory to the returned graph, pcalg's is the transfer into R, cor(X), and the call; ratio is the median over the paired datasets of pcalg's time over Andrey's | BOSS-FCI/GRaSP-FCI: per dataset, each package in one child process pinned to one core with one BLAS thread; Andrey runs each fit once untimed on the same data first, and Tetrad starts one JVM per run with one untimed warm-up search before the timed one; each Tetrad hybrid runs five times per dataset with no seed (once on the 200-variable cell); a call past its cap (1,800 s; 3,600 s at 100 variables and out of claim) is a timeout, never an empty graph; Andrey's time is the fit from the array in memory, Tetrad's the search inside the JVM; ratio is the median over the paired datasets of the reference's time over Andrey's | J-PCMCI+: each fit in a fresh interpreter on one core with one BLAS thread, after one untimed warm-up fit (none with GPDC, nor for tigramite above 5 system variables, where a fit runs for minutes); a cap of 1,800 s and 16,000 MB per fit with imports and warm-up, past which a fit is a timeout, never an empty graph; each package's time runs from the datasets in memory to the returned graph, tigramite's including its dummies and DataFrame; ratio is the median over the paired draws of tigramite's time over Andrey's
error_metric: FCI-JCI: shd: the endpoint SHD over the data variables and the environment against FCI-JCI's PAG at the true distribution under the same assumptions: variable pairs whose two endpoint marks differ, so a missing or extra edge costs both. andrey_shd, comparator_shd, and empty_shd are medians over the paired datasets, and the _mean fields their means | BOSS-FCI/GRaSP-FCI: shd: the endpoint SHD against the PAG of the measured variables (andrey.data.latent.marginal, checked against pcalg's dag2pag on every graph of up to 30 measured variables): variable pairs whose two endpoint marks differ, so a missing or extra edge costs both. andrey_shd, comparator_shd, and empty_shd are medians over the paired datasets, the reference's SHD per dataset the mean over its runs, and the _mean fields their means | J-PCMCI+: shd: the endpoint SHD over the links between system variables at lags 0 to 2: a missing or extra link costs its two marks, a wrong mark one; for the entries named context links, the links from the observed contexts into the system variables that a fit misses plus those it adds. andrey_errors, comparator_errors, and empty_errors are medians over the paired draws, the _shd_mean fields their means, and andrey_adjacency_f1 and comparator_adjacency_f1 the mean F1 of the links between system variables, whatever their marks
complete_definition: FCI-JCI: true when every setting has at least 10 paired datasets (both packages finished); a setting with fewer is listed in incomplete, its timeouts counted and never scored | BOSS-FCI/GRaSP-FCI: true when every row has at least 10 paired datasets (both packages finished); a row with fewer is listed in incomplete, its timeouts counted and never scored | J-PCMCI+: true when every row has at least 10 paired draws (both packages finished) and no planned fit is pending; a row with fewer is listed in incomplete
seeds_note: FCI-JCI: seeds is the number of datasets per setting: 20 (seeds 0-19) in every cell but P20 and P50, which ran 10 (seeds 0-9). pcalg was not run on P50, X100, X100m: on the dry run's two datasets of each (seeds 0 and 1), every pcalg fit, at both assumption sets and every level, timed out at the 1,800 s cap, and the campaign runs pcalg on such a cell only where it finished a dry-run fit; Andrey's rows there are reported against the empty graph. No in-claim row came out better or worse, so no rerun ran | BOSS-FCI/GRaSP-FCI: seeds is the number of datasets per cell on the first seeds: 20 (seeds 0-19) in P20 and P100, 10 (seeds 0-9) in O1 and O3, and 1 (seed 0) in O2, which measures time only. 10 cells with a row better or worse on the first seeds reran both packages' gated arms on seeds 100-119 (replication); 17 cells with an edge_removal="triangles" row better or worse on the first seeds reran that arm and causal-cmd's on seeds 100-119 | J-PCMCI+: seeds is the number of draws in the row, each one seed's datasets: every cell runs seeds 0-19, and the cells with a hidden context seeds 0-39, split into the draws where Assumption 3 holds and those where it breaks. No in-claim row came out better or worse, so no rerun ran
